nodes.title: Nonunital and augmented algebras
nodes.statement: For each commutative R, construct an equivalence from nonunital commutative R-algebras to augmented commutative R-algebras. Send I to the existing Unitization R I with augmentation (r,x)↦r; send an augmentation A→R to its kernel. The unit and counit are natural algebra isomorphisms. Bundle this category over the existing carriers and nonunital algebra homomorphisms; its forgetful functor creates limits and sifted colimits. The augmentation ideal of R[X_s] is free on the set of variables.
hypotheses: Rings are commutative with identity unless explicitly nonunital; spectral and coefficient conventions are those in the reader introduction.
proofSteps: Use Unitization.lift for the forward map on morphisms.
For an augmentation ε, decompose a as the scalar ε(a) plus an element of ker ε; prove both inverse identities and naturality.
acceptance: The multiplication is (r,x)(s,y)=(rs,ry+sx+xy), including the xy term.

nodes.title: Local nonunital algebras
nodes.statement: A nonunital commutative algebra I is local in the nonunital sense if for every x∈I there is y∈I with x+y+xy=0. Prove uniqueness of y and equivalence to 1+x being a unit in R⋉I for every x, hence to I lying in the Jacobson radical of R⋉I. This adjective does not assert that R⋉I is a local ring.
hypotheses: Rings are commutative with identity unless explicitly nonunital; spectral and coefficient conventions are those in the reader introduction.
proofSteps: Multiply (1+x)(1+y) and use uniqueness of inverses.
An element of the augmentation kernel is radical precisely when all its scalar multiples have 1 minus that element invertible.
acceptance: For I=0 over R=Z, the condition holds although its unitization Z is not local.

nodes.title: Henselian nonunital algebras
nodes.statement: A nonunital commutative R-algebra I is henselian if, for every n≥1 and g∈I[T], the equation T(1+T)^{n−1}+g(T)=0 has a unique solution in I. Interpret g by evaluation in the unitization, with coefficients in its augmentation ideal. This notion is independent of R and implies local nonunitality.
hypotheses: Rings are commutative with identity unless explicitly nonunital; spectral and coefficient conventions are those in the reader introduction.
proofSteps: Apply the simple-root characterization of henselian pairs to the displayed polynomial at zero.
Translate the converse polynomial factor-lifting criterion through the augmentation kernel; n=1 alone is not the definition.
acceptance: For an ideal I⊂A, the intrinsic definition agrees with HenselianRing A I (the ambient-independence theorem below).

nodes.title: Henselian algebra limits and quotients
nodes.statement: The forgetful functor from henselian nonunital R-algebras to sets creates limits and sifted colimits. Quotients of a henselian nonunital algebra by any ideal are henselian. Changing the scalar ring along a compatible action does not change intrinsic henselianity.
hypotheses: Rings are commutative with identity unless explicitly nonunital; spectral and coefficient conventions are those in the reader introduction.
proofSteps: Encode each unique root as a finitary operation, so equations are preserved by limits and sifted colimits.
For a quotient lift finitely many coefficients to I, solve there and descend; uniqueness is inherited from the simple-root factor criterion.
acceptance: Filtered colimits need no common nilpotence exponent.

nodes.title: Henselian reflection and finite free projectives
nodes.statement: The full inclusion of henselian nonunital R-algebras admits a left adjoint I↦Iʰ. Let R{X_s}⁺ be the reflection of the augmentation ideal of R[X_s]. It is free on the set of generators. This category is the category of models of a finitary algebraic theory; its compact projective objects are precisely retracts of free objects on finite sets. Here projectivity means lifting against surjective algebra maps, and compactness means preservation of filtered colimits by the set-valued Hom functor.
hypotheses: Rings are commutative with identity unless explicitly nonunital; spectral and coefficient conventions are those in the reader introduction.
proofSteps: Use orthogonality to the finite-presentation maps encoding root existence and uniqueness, or henselize the augmented pair.
The free/forgetful adjunction and the finitary operations give monadicity; finite free objects are compact projective and projective presentations split to give the retract characterization.
acceptance: The free functor is a left adjoint; do not reverse this variance.

Base change those neighborhoods through the Milnor pushout; the universal property identifies the resulting henselizations.

nodes.title: Connectivity of topological cyclic homology
nodes.statement: For a p-complete cyclotomic spectrum X with underlying spectrum in Sp≥n, TC(X) lies in Sp≥n−1. In particular TC/p on connective cyclotomic spectra preserves geometric realizations.

Supply w-local refinement: closed points form a closed subset and each connected component has one closed point; affine schemes admit the w-local refinements used to split finite Zariski covers, and their finite-projective/K1/K2 formulas reduce by filtered limits to finite products of local rings.

Construct étale Postnikov sheafification K̂_et as lim_n a_et τ≤n K with the trace-compatible descent spectral sequence. Supply Nisnevich descent and reduction of homotopy-invariant henselian-rigid K-theory fibre bounds to residue fields on finite-dimensional characteristic-p schemes (CMM Theorem 6.5, pp. 52–53). Keep the field p-rank bound [k:k^p]≤p^d uniform and use only the resulting n≥d range; no statement of unbounded étale cohomological convergence is assumed.

For characteristic-p commutative rings, identify absolute Frobenius pullback with ψ^p on K-theory and prove the integral Adams-filtration consequence: for a perfect F_p-algebra A, K_i(A) is uniquely p-divisible for i>0, and the kernel of the rank map K0(A)→locally constant integer-valued functions is uniquely p-divisible. Include passage from connected finite-type perfections to arbitrary perfect algebras using filtered colimits and Zariski descent, as in CMM Example 6.8, p. 53. A rational eigenspace theorem alone does not imply these assertions.

For a connective finite-type spectrum such as S/p, each bounded Postnikov truncation belongs to the thick subcategory generated by HF_p if its homotopy groups are finite p-groups. Supply finite-type Postnikov approximations to HZ, the stable Hurewicz theorem identifying the bottom nonzero homotopy with integral homology, and Freudenthal connectivity for Σ∞K(A,n)→Σ^nHA uniformly in A. For free finite-rank A, the bar/cellular construction of K(A,n) has finitely many cells in each bounded degree. These uniform estimates, rather than pointwise compactness, are the needed inputs.

Countable Mittag–Leffler criterion: an inverse sequence of abelian groups with vanishing lim¹ of its countable direct sum is Mittag–Leffler. Apply pointwise, then use preservation of countable coproducts and a diagonal choice of witnesses to obtain a single transition annihilating a fixed tower level as a natural transformation. The finite-range spectral version uses the Milnor exact sequence degree by degree with one common range [a,b].

restructure.detail: The three henselian routes share one proof and are merged here. The nine CMM §5.2 items extend the independent AMMN deformation-of-classes direction already identified by the extractions. Keeping them separate makes henselian rigidity an input to tower continuity, avoiding two owners for the same p-adic deformation result.

retained.title: Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods, Part II: henselian pairs
retained.owns: Finite-coefficient cyclotomic continuity, nonunital henselian algebra, pseudocoherent trace-fibre rigidity, F-finite I-adic continuity, pro logarithmic comparisons and the étale/quasisyntomic K consequences.

separate.title: Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods, Part II: p-adic deformation of K-theory classes

stages.title: Uniformly controlled inverse towers
stages.targets: Nilpotent and quickly converging towers; almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers defined by upper truncations; finite Postnikov dévissage under a common lower bound; closure under the tensor products in CMM Lemmas 5.13, 5.15–5.18.
stages.negativeTest: The tower ⊕_(j≥i)Σ^(−j)HF_p has degreewise zero pro homotopy and is not almost nilpotent.

stages.title: Derived p-adic continuity of TC
stages.targets: CMM Theorem 5.19 for connective E1-ring towers whose mod-p underlying tower is almost quickly converging; Theorem 5.20 for HZ-algebras and derived p-power quotients. Retain map-level comparisons and the restriction/Frobenius operations.

stages.title: Derived p-adic continuity of K and deformation
stages.targets: CMM Theorems 5.21–5.22: derived quotients for connective HZ-algebras with commutative π0 henselian along p, and ordinary p-power quotients for discrete henselian rings with bounded p-power torsion; Remark 5.23 over the sphere. Supply the AMMN continuous K/TC inputs. Compare K^inv only modulo p after DGM and HP.5 rigidity.
tests: A ring with unbounded p-power torsion to show the ordinary-quotient theorem does not apply

separate.boundary: Imports HP.1 connective tower limits and finite-coefficient TC continuity, HP.5 henselian trace rigidity and base RT.2/RT.3. Does not own HP.6 F-finite arbitrary-I continuity or repeat the proof of henselian rigidity. Merge this assignment into the AMMN design when that route is scheduled.

sources.match: The inverse-tower continuity argument is independent of the finite-approximation proof except for the explicitly listed imports.

upstreamNotes.note: Its henselian trace-square export should import HP.5/henselian-trace-rigidity. This Part II does not import that export, avoiding a proof cycle. Its first-derivative Goodwillie node does not supply the whole suspension–loop tower.

Current Tau Ceti already lifts ordinary idempotents along henselian ideals. HP.3 plans the residual finite-projective module isomorphism-class and K0 consequences using henselian smooth lifting for the idempotent-matrix scheme, not a second ordinary idempotent-lifting theory.

The extraction mentions logarithmic coefficients here; the reusable classical/logarithmic de Rham–Witt groups and their finite-level exact sequences are imported from CrystallineCohomology:CR.4, so a second coefficient theory is not planned.
